abstract: One hundred adnexal masses were discovered at the time of pregnancy termination among a total of 55,278 pregnancy terminations performed at the Los Angeles County/University of Southern California Medical Center between 1970 and 1982. Seven patients were found to be not pregnant, and 93 masses were associated with pregnancy, for an incidence of one adnexal mass for every 594 (0.17%) terminations. Benign cystic teratoma was the most common lesion found (46;50%). There were two (2.2%) ovarian malignancies, 15 masses were bilateral, 11 masses were associated with pain, and torsion of the adnexa had occurred in seven cases. The preoperative diagnosis was made more commonly in the first trimester (86%) than in the second trimester (29%). Since many ovarian tumors are small, the true incidence is unknown. In a series of 998 abortion hysterectomies, 13 ovarian tumors were found, for an incidence of 1.3%.
abstract_ja: 1970年から1982年にかけて、ロサンゼルス郡／南カリフォルニア大学医療センターで行われた55,278件の妊娠中絶のうち、100例の付属器腫瘤が妊娠中絶時に発見された。非妊娠であった7例を除く93例の腫瘤は妊娠に関連しており、妊娠中絶約594件に1件（0.17%）の割合で付属器腫瘤がみられた。最も多い病変は良性嚢胞性奇形腫であった（46例、50%）。悪性腫瘍は2例（2.2%）であった。15例は両側性で、11例は疼痛を伴い、7例では付属器捻転が生じていた。術前診断は妊娠初期（86%）の方が妊娠中期（29%）よりも多くなされた。多くの卵巣腫瘍は小さいため、真の発生率は不明である。998件の妊娠中絶子宮摘出術の系列では、13例の卵巣腫瘍が発見され、発生率は1.3%であった。
